reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: India's AI summit and responsible-use approach
themes.definition: The speaker's country presents its own AI leadership, summit hosting, or national approach to harnessing AI.
themes.inclusion: Passages citing hosting of AI summits, G20 AI initiatives, or a national approach to AI deployment.
themes.exclusion: Passages about other national achievements (digital public infrastructure, startups) that do not mention AI.
themes.boundary_cases: A G20 outcome on responsible AI listed among many initiatives can be coded both here and as a list mention.

examples.quote: India hosted the AI Impact Summit this February, gathering together the best minds on that subject.
India's approach is to harness it responsibly for human welfare. Inclusion and impact will be the watchwords for the summit that India will host in 2026.

themes.label: AI for development and human empowerment
themes.definition: AI framed as a driver of development, human welfare, economic prosperity and large-scale problem solving.
themes.inclusion: Passages describing AI's promise for development, human empowerment or population-scale problem solving.
themes.exclusion: Passages about AI risk or misuse.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements about harnessing AI 'responsibly' still count here when the focus is development benefit.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence as a horizontal and cross-cutting technology has a particular promise for development.
We view AI as a transformational driver for human empowerment, economic prosperity, and population-scale problem solving.

themes.label: Right to national AI models
themes.definition: Each nation's right to shape its own AI ecosystem and models, set against technology withholding and choke points.
themes.inclusion: Passages asserting national rights to develop own AI models or objecting to technology denial and choke points.
themes.exclusion: Passages about national AI achievements with no sovereignty or dependence argument.
themes.boundary_cases: Complaints about 'withholding technology' without naming AI can be coded here only when adjacent to AI discussion.

examples.quote: We believe in the right of each nation to shape its ecosystem with the development of its own models and deployment strategies

themes.label: AI partnership with the Global South
themes.definition: AI as part of partnership, sharing and democratization agendas with developing countries.
themes.inclusion: Passages promising AI cooperation, sharing tools, or democratizing technology for the Global South.
themes.exclusion: General development assistance not tied to AI or technology.
themes.boundary_cases: Sharing digital public infrastructure without AI mention does not count.

examples.quote: AI will be very much part of a partnership agenda with the global South.

themes.label: AI misuse sharpening bias
themes.definition: Brief warnings that misuse of AI sharpens bias and erodes mutual respect, turning technology from hope into anxiety.
themes.inclusion: Passages stating AI misuse increases bias, division or anxiety.
themes.boundary_cases: Could overlap with ethics; code here when the harm is framed as misuse sharpening social or international bias.

examples.quote: Misuse of AI is sharpening bias and diluting mutual respect.

themes.label: Responsible AI listed among G20 outcomes
themes.definition: AI named as one item in a list of policy initiatives or concerns without elaboration.
themes.inclusion: Passages where responsible AI is one entry in a list of summit outcomes or initiatives.
themes.exclusion: Passages elaborating AI's effects or governance.
themes.boundary_cases: If the list item is later elaborated in the same passage, code the substantive theme.

examples.quote: Others focus on new concerns, such as the responsible harnessing of artificial intelligence.

value.rationale: All Indian passages; AI is mainly framed as a development and empowerment tool tied to India's summit leadership and Global South partnership, with a sovereignty claim to national models, a brief warning about misuse sharpening bias, and a 2023 list-style G20 mention.
